ai.description: *Raorchestes sahai* is a small bush frog (SVL ~20–25 mm) with a brown dorsum and distinct dark interorbital markings. It features granular skin and lacks a vocal sac.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Raorchestes sahai* is best distinguished by the distinct, bright yellow or orange webbing between its toes, a feature absent in most other similar bush frogs.
ai.habitat: The Sahai Bush Frog inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 1,500 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Sahai bush frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden within dense vegetation during the day and emerging at night to forage for small insects among the foliage.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes sahai* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It lays terrestrial eggs during the monsoon season (June–August) in vegetation or tree holes.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Sahai Bush Frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically inhabiting the high-altitude shola forests of Kerala and Tamil Nadu above 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Sahai Bush Frog emits a high-pitched, insect-like series of rapid, rhythmic pulses, typically heard from vegetation in high-altitude forest habitats.
